### Jesus Was Forsaken for Us
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-march-29-2022.html
Passage: Psalm 22:1
Points:
- Jesus became the true sin-bearer when He went to the cross on our behalf.
- A holy God turned His face away from sin, subjecting Jesus to the penalty of forsakenness.
- David knew God was with him through the dark valley, but Jesus walked that valley alone.
- Christ endured total abandonment so that His followers will never be forsaken by God.
- Meditating on the Lord's sacrifice should compel believers to share His love with others.

### He Will Restore Your Soul
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/he-will-restore-your-soul
Passage: Psalm 22:1
Points:
- Believers frequently experience the painful feeling of God's silence during deep trials.
- On the cross, Jesus bore our unholy sin and endured actual, horrifying separation from the Father.
- Christ suffered the curse of divine wrath so that believers would receive eternal mercy.
- Jesus intimately understands our loneliness and weakness because His suffering exceeded ours.
- The cost paid in Psalm 22 purchases the eternal soul restoration celebrated in Psalm 23.

### Wisdom from the Psalms 3/1
Author: Wisdom from the Psalms
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/wisdom/wisdom-from-the-psalms-3-or-1-552178.html
Passage: Psalm 22:21
Points:
- Seasons of danger and spiritual darkness can leave believers feeling isolated and afraid.
- The presence of God's Word brings tangible security and comfort during frightening moments.
- The Lord draws near to protect and deliver those who cry out under threat.
- Believers can replace panic with rest by trusting in God's power to save.

### The Suffering and the Glory of Psalm 22
Author: W. Robert Godfrey
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/suffering-and-glory-psalm-22
Passage: Psalm 22:1-31
Points:
- Feeling abandoned by God in times of trouble is a frequent struggle for the faithful.
- David responded to distress not with despair, but by praying and recalling God's past mercies.
- The psalm prophetically portrays the agony, piercing, and substitutionary sacrifice of Christ.
- The agony of the cross dramatically transforms into global and multi-generational worship.
- Believers learn a pattern of piety: moving from earthly trouble through prayer to ultimate praise.
